subject: Recap: Dedicated GPU fit discovery — Finnova (next steps & checklist)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sara Malik <sara@finnova.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Dedicated GPU fit discovery — Finnova (next steps & checklist)

Sara — thanks again for taking the time today. High-level recap from our call and clear next steps so we stay aligned.

Key pain points you shared:
- Production inference unpredictability: spikes in concurrent requests cause 2-3x latency increases during peak windows.
- Cost variability when falling back to public hosted endpoints for burst traffic.
- Regulatory requirement for tenant isolation and customer data encryption-at-rest; SOC 2 in progress.
- Need deterministic capacity for SLAs (billing team requires predictable burn).

Current stack (as discussed):
- Primary: on-prem GPU cluster (NVIDIA A100-ish) behind a Kubernetes layer; custom batching layer.
- Fallback: public LLM API for overflow requests during spikes.
- Observability: Prometheus for infra metrics, Datadog for app traces.

Success criteria for a Dedicated deployment:
- Sustained throughput: support baseline 1,200 TPS inference requests (avg payload) with p95 latency target <= 250ms.
- Burst capability: absorb 3x baseline for at least 5 minutes with graceful degradation.
- Isolation: customer-dedicated pools and separated KV cache; customer-managed keys preferred.
- Cost predictability: monthly committed capacity with clear overage/burst pricing.

Immediate next steps (action items):
1) Please review the attached "Redwood_Dedicated_Technical_Checklist.pdf" and return any missing environment details (networking, KMS, allowed egress).
2) Finnova: share 24h sample request distribution (timestamps + qps) or a synthesized request profile to calibrate pooling and batching assumptions.
3) Redwood: we will provide an initial capacity sizing and a draft SoW (attachment) by EOD next Thursday (May 24).
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive (30–45m) with Finnova infra + our SRE/SEs — proposed slots in the checklist.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Technical_Checklist.pdf (checklist + required network ports)

If any of the above items are off-base, flag them and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll follow up with the sizing and a proposed meeting invite for 5/24.

Thanks — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

From: Sara Malik <sara@finnova.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated GPU fit discovery — Finnova (next steps & checklist)

Thanks Hannah — this is a very accurate recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- The baseline we quoted is ~1,200 requests/minute (not TPS) — apologies for mixing units on the call. Peak windows reach ~4,000 requests/minute for 3–7 minute bursts during end-of-day processing.
- Isolation: we need customer-dedicated pools (no shared tenancy) and a separated KV cache per tenant; BYOK with an HSM-backed KMS is preferred.
- SOC 2: currently in Type I, target Type II in Q4; we can provide the SOC 2 Type I report to expedite review.

On deliverables:
- I’ll attach a 24h sample of request timestamps and a synthetic request profile by EOD tomorrow.
- Would appreciate a preliminary run-rate estimate (committed vs burst pricing) in the SoW draft you mentioned.

Proposed next call: May 24, 11:00–11:45 PT — can your SRE and solutions engineer join?

Best,
Sara

Subject: Internal: Finnova sizing notes

Quick internal thread — adding my notes after the call.
- Use Finnova's corrected numbers: baseline 1,200 req/minute ~20 req/sec, peak 4,000 req/min (~67 req/sec).
- For p95 <= 250ms with batching and reserved A100-class pool, propose a baseline pool sized for sustained 80 req/sec with 1.5x headroom => initial reserved capacity ~120 req/sec equivalent.
- Burst policy: allow autoscale to 3x reserved for 7 minutes with graceful shedding and fallback to regional hosted model (configurable). Confirm marketing/legal on pricing for burst overage.
- Network/egress: need to validate Finnova's allowed outbound IP ranges and any private-link requirement.
- Action items for SE (Evelyn): generate a cost / capacity matrix (baseline vs burst vs on-demand) and prepare a brief runbook for failover behavior.
- HubSpot: attach proposed deal id FIN-2026-045 and include proposed SoW template link (see hubspot link).

Dylan
Solutions Engineer (on call)
